{{short description|Spanish physicist}}
'''Beatriz Roldán Cuenya''' (born 1976 in [[Oviedo]]) is a [[Spaniards|Spanish]] [[physicist]] working in [[surface science]] and [[catalysis]]. Since 2017, she has been director of the Department of Interface Science at the [[Fritz Haber Institute]] of the [[Max Planck Society]] in [[Berlin]], Germany. Since April 2023, she has also been interim director of the Department of Inorganic Chemistry, also at the Fritz Haber Institute.

== Professional career ==

Roldán Cuenya studied at the [[University of Oviedo]] in Spain and received her doctorate degree from the [[University of Duisburg-Essen]] in Germany under the supervision of 
Werner Keune.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Appreciation for Werner Keune |url=https://www.fhi.mpg.de/742615/2021-03-30_Keune_Appreciation |access-date=2022-12-15 |website=www.fhi.mpg.de |language=en}}</ref> As a postdoc she worked at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] in the group of Eric McFarland and subsequently became professor at the [[University of Central Florida]] in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]] (USA).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sciences.ucf.edu/physics/people/cuenya-beatriz-roldan/|title=Roldan Cuenya, Beatriz – at University of Central Florida, Physics Department|work=Physics|access-date=2018-06-15|language=en-US}}</ref> In 2013, she accepted a Chair Faculty position in Solid State Physics at the [[Ruhr University Bochum]] in Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ep4.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/|title=Institute for Experimental Physics IV – EP4|last=Termer|first=Evgenij|website=www.ep4.ruhr-uni-bochum.de|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-06-15}}</ref> She holds two roles at the Fritz Haber Institute - since 2017 as Director of the Department of Interface Science, and since April 2023 as interim Director of the Department of Inorganic Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fhi.mpg.de/isc-department/director|title=FHI|last=PPB|first=Fritz-Haber-Institut|website=www.fhi-berlin.mpg.de|access-date=7 March 2024}}</ref>

Her main research interests are the synthesis of [[nanostructure]]d materials with tunable surface properties and the experimental investigation of structure-reactivity relationships in thermal and electro-catalysis using ''[[in situ]]'' and [[Operando spectroscopy|''operando'']] methods. Applications of her work are in the areas of [[environmental remediation]] and energy conversion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Beatriz_Roldan_Cuenya|title=Beatriz Roldan Cuenya {{!}} PhD {{!}} Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society, Berlin {{!}} FHI {{!}} Department of Interface Science|last=PhD|first=Beatriz Roldan CuenyaFritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society {{!}} FHI · Department of Interface Science 40 87 ·|website=ResearchGate|language=en|access-date=2018-06-17}}</ref>
